brief: AI-driven investment and loose fiscal policy keep demand resilient, keeping the neutral rate elevated, so the Fed hiked again and signalled a cycle rather than a one-off move: the new dot plot shows one more hike in 2026, rates flat through 2027, and 17 of 18 members still see inflation risk skewed higher. Resilient growth plus higher energy prices from the Middle East conflict have pushed 10-year Treasury yields above 5%, the highest since 2007; J. Safra Sarasin's fair-value range is 4.5-5%, based on a 3.5-4% neutral rate, so yields stay elevated only if inflation converges to target on schedule. Widening G10 rate differentials have weakened the Swiss franc, but rising odds that the SNB hikes sooner than markets expect, plus political risks (US midterms, French election), could trigger a franc rebound and a reversal of CHF-funded carry trades. Global industrials suffered their sharpest six-month underperformance since 2020 on AI-trade exhaustion, oil-hit airlines and a European defence pullback, but earnings momentum stayed the second-strongest of any sector and accelerating German defence spending (up 30% year-to-date) should let headwinds fade.
